_about: Our render decisions layered over the researched specs. Researched numbers are never edited here; every override says why. House safe zones apply only where the platform publishes none, and the report labels them.

pinterest.pin.standard.why: Pinterest's 270/790 safe zone is published for full-screen 9:16 pins; it does not apply to a 2:3 feed pin.

tiktok.ads.spark.why: Spark Ads boost an organic post; we render the video variant (carousel Spark is the photo-mode carousel).

youtube.channel.watermark.why: The watermark is a 150px brand mark, rendered like a profile image.

google.display.responsive.logo_wide.why: 4:1 logo slot: tile + wordmark, not a square avatar.

snapchat.ads.story_tile.why: The Story tile is a small vertical ad (image + headline), not a logo.

instagram.reels.cover.why: The Reels cover is the reel's thumbnail; the grid shows its centre 3:4.

linkedin.ad.conversation.why: 300x250 banner shown beside a message ad.

linkedin.ad.message.why: 300x250 banner shown beside a message ad.

instagram.profile.grid_preview.why: Not an upload: it is how the profile grid crops feed posts (3:4). Enforced as a crop on feed formats instead.

house_safe_zones._why: Platforms that publish no pixel safe zone still cover the frame with UI. These are conservative margins we hold until an official figure exists; the export report marks every asset that uses one.

tiktok.feed.video.note: house: TikTok publishes its ad safe zone only as a downloadable template; right rail = like/comment/share, bottom = caption + music

tiktok.ads.in_feed.video.note: house: same as organic feed until the official template is read

youtube.shorts.video.note: house: YouTube publishes no Shorts safe zone; right rail + title/channel at the bottom

crops._why: Places a platform shows a cropped view of the asset. Text must sit inside the crop too; merged with the safe zone (larger margin wins).

instagram.feed.portrait.note: profile grid shows feed posts as 3:4 tiles (Instagram Help Center, 2025)

instagram.feed.carousel.note: profile grid 3:4 tile shows the first card

instagram.feed.square.note: profile grid 3:4 tile crops the square's sides

instagram.ad.feed.image.note: boosted/feed images also appear in the 3:4 grid
